title: Request: make `md_document()` support TOC (table of content)
description:
I'm using {hugodown} to render blog posts on my website. With longer blog posts it would be great to have the option to include a table of content (TOC), which is, to my understanding, not possible with `hugodown::md_document()`. 

I thought a viable workaround would be to replace `hugodown::md_document()` with `rmarkdown::md_document()`. However, this led to rendering problems. 

I then took the relevant code from `rmarkdown::md_document()` and included it in my forked version of {hugodown} in the [toc branch](https://github.com/TimTeaFan/hugodown/tree/toc).

I do understand that {hugodown} is focused on a streamlined, highly minimal HTML output and adding a TOC might contradict this philosophy - in this case please close this issue. Otherwise I'd happily PR the branch.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: R code bocks are always collapsed
description:
Hi there! I'm having a bit of trouble making hugodown produce code blocks that aren't collapsed (R code a different block as the eval result). Say that I have the following R code block: ```{r, collapse=FALSE} # loading and checking the data print("mensagem") ``` This will generate the following MD: ``` 
# loading and checking the data
print("mensagem")
#> [1] "mensagem"
``` What I would like is to have them in separate `div`s. I'm able to achieve that by having two separate code blocks: ```{r, eval=FALSE} # loading and checking the data print("mensagem") ``` ```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE} # loading and checking the data print("mensagem") ``` Which will yield me ``` 
# loading and checking the data
print("mensagem")
#> [1] "mensagem"
``` How can I achieve the same result without having to use two separate code blocks? Thanks!!

title: How to use images in blog posts?
description:
Thanks for this cool package. I could not find a reference to how to embed an image stored somewhere in the repo in a post and standard blogdown approach did not work. 

I put some images in `static` and reference them relative to the location of my post in `content/posts/post-xyz`, i.e. with `../../static/post/post-xyz/...`. Rendering with {knitr} works. But then, `hugodown::hugo_start()` renders md to html, and the paths are wrong (I believe because the working directory is a different one) and images are not displayed. I manually changed the paths in the `.md` after knitting to be relative to the root (`/post/post-xyz/...`), as all static content is placed there, and then they were displayed correctly, but that's a bit of a hack. 

I was not sure if I hit a limitation described in the README, but I felt probably it's something else:

> It does not currently support within page cross-references for figures, tables, and equations.

title: Add caption-hiding option à la html_document
description:
Per discussion with @jennybc, and somewhat related to https://github.com/r-lib/hugodown/issues/79, it would be nice to:
1. Ultimately separate out what constitutes a caption vs alt-text (since they're not really the same)—though that might be something worth addressing upstream in the rmarkdown stack.
2. In the meantime, add the option as it currently exists for `html_document` to hide or show the caption using `fig_caption: false` in the yaml (see [bookdown docs here](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/html-accessibility.html)).

Closest thing I found in rmarkdonw/knitr stack was https://github.com/yihui/knitr/commit/42b91f01608e573e6c255e3adacf0f75bccdb176

title: Hugo executable not successfully located on macOS
description:
With latest master(97ea0cdd63152a58987ae9e2639bcc4db4e5a83a), I get

```r
> hugodown::hugo_start()
Starting server on port 1313
Error: hugo 0.59.1 not installed
ℹ Do you need to call `hugodown::hugo_install('0.59.1')`?
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
> hugodown::hugo_install('0.59.1')
Finding release
hugo 0.59.1 already installed
> hugodown::hugo_start()
Starting server on port 1313
Error: hugo 0.59.1 not installed
ℹ Do you need to call `hugodown::hugo_install('0.59.1')`?
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
```

Turns out that the directory structure on macOS is
```
~/Library/Caches/hugodown/hugo_extended_0.59.1_macOS_64bit/hugo
```
So in `hugo_locate()`, we should probably check if the *directory* `~/Library/Caches/hugodown/hugo_extended_0.59.1_macOS_64bit` exists, not the file.

title: Fails to deploy when using embracing operator {{}} for tidy eval
description:
Working on a new blog post and kept getting an error when deploying:

`Error: Error building site: "/opt/build/repo/content/post/test_post/index.md:60:38": failed to extract shortcode: template for shortcode "span" not found`

After a bit of experimentation I think this is a problem with how syntax highlighting treats the {{}}. Putting the code below into a hugodown post will reproduce this error .
```
library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(
  x = 1:4,
  y = c("a", "a", "b", "b")

)

make_groups <- function(df, group_var){
  df <- df %>%
    group_by({{group_var}}) %>%
    summarize(mean = mean(x))
}

df <- df %>%
  make_groups(y)

df
```

title: No but actually how do I programmatically knit a single hugodown post?
description:
Oh wizards of hugodown, I beseech thee! No disrespect to RStudio but sometimes I want to knit my hugodown posts from other IDEs, or even from the command-line via `Rscript`.
Currently [the documentation](https://hugodown.r-lib.org/#usage) tells us

>To knit an .Rmd post, you can use the Knit button to knit to the correct output format. You can also use the keyboard shortcut Cmd+Shift+K (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+K (Windows/Linux).

This unfortunately makes sense only in RStudio and does not give me the information I need to knit the post programatically. I'm presuming it is something obvious such as `knitr::knit("content/notebook/levy_processes.Rmd")` but that does not seem to pick up the right config and renders the markdown output in the current directory rather than next to the post where it belongs.
I expect it is a small change to make this work, but I do not know what it is.
But armed with this information I could add hugodown support to other IDEs (e.g.  [VSCode](https://github.com/TianyiShi2001/rmarkdown-vscode)) and to my own build scripts. And even put it in the documentation of this fine project.

title: is it worth exporting hugo_locate?
description:
I wonder if it would be worth exporting `hugo_locate()`? It's a handy function to use if you're writing a wrapper function that creates sites using a different Hugo theme. At the moment I'm accessing it via `:::` in the slumdown package, but it would be nice to avoid the inevitable warning message on R CMD check:

https://github.com/djnavarro/slumdown/blob/master/R/install_hugodown.R#L16

Alternative options I'm considering:

- I could write a PR to add a `create_site_slum()` function to hugodown instead of having slumdown as a distinct package
- I could mirror `hugo_locate()` and the many internal functions it calls inside slumdown

title: Adding more docs for citations?
description:
Might be too niche. I was thinking that some users might want to use a site-wide CSL, and even a site-wide bibliography ([it was asked in the issue tracker of `distill`](https://github.com/rstudio/distill/issues/82)).

It's easy to get and I wonder whether it should be documented, maybe in an article about bibliographies.

* save the CSL and/or bib at the root for instance.
* in the archetype (since there's no site config for hugodown, just individual Rmds), add

```
bibliography: ../../../refs.bib
suppress-bibliography: true
csl: ../../../chicago-fullnote-bibliography.csl
```

I've just tested it.

title: Code chunks other than R rendered as NA
description:
When I use languages other than R, the input _sometimes_ appears as NA, although the output is unaffected. I've been able to replicate this with python, bash and scala.

In terms of a reproducible example, I've created a new hugodown site using the latest version of hugodown, and the function `create_site_academic()`. I created [an R Markdown file with code chunks from these languages](https://github.com/mdneuzerling/test-site/blob/prime/content/post/test/index.Rmd). I then knitted [the markdown file which shows the NA inputs](https://github.com/mdneuzerling/test-site/blob/prime/content/post/test/index.md).

I'm happy to give this issue a go and try to find the cause as best I can. Thus far I've tried using another machine (Windows, without the bash chunk), and disabling `link_inline`. I think a hint here is that in the Python code chunk, `print("This is a python chunk")` isn't converted to `NA`. I suspect this is because that line is also valid R code.

title: Move custom hugodown Rmd archetype to project root
description: Currently with `create_site_academic()` the function overwrites the default post archetype with an `index.Rmd` file in: `themes/academic/archetypes/post/`. But, if a user updates their Hugo theme (which is recommended periodically), this archetype will be overwritten. Would you consider instead writing to `archetypes/post/` in the project root? That would be more robust, and encourage good practices w/r/t updating themes when running into errors (just like we encourage folks to update their R packages).

title: Suggestions for Netlify template & docs
description:
* The screenshots are missing from the vignette.

* Could the template feature different settings for previews and production, e.g. [only build future posts in a preview](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse.org/blob/a441f91751c50d1d98c47795220b8f7202bded29/netlify.toml#L16)? And/or could the docs explain that? "Common useful variations of the Netlify config".

* Could the docs (of the Netlify function, of the vignette) explicitly say what "--baseURL $DEPLOY_PRIME_URL" does? (as Details?) "This option ensures relative links to other pages of your site, e.g. `See [my recent post](/post/recent-post)`, will be rendered by Hugo as links to your site as built in the preview (`https://deploy-preview-692--blabla.netlify.app/post/recent-post`), not your site as deployed in production (_not_ `https://hugodown.org/post/recent-post`), which is useful when you change and check something site-wide such as stylesheets".

* And shouldn't this option above only be used for PRs?

title: Option to turn off downlit?
description:
Could `md_document` gain an argument to not apply `downlit` ?

There was previously an option with [`hugo_document` to switch on `downlit`](https://github.com/r-lib/hugodown/blob/283750354f21f24686b6a4173bf79264f4cc1a9e/R/hugo-format.R#L23)

However it looks like that option has been removed now in [`md_document`](https://github.com/r-lib/hugodown/blob/master/R/hugo-format.R).

While I think that downlit is awesome, and I love the idea, at the moment I don't want to generate links to functions, as it seems to change the colours I get. Here's an example of what I meant:

Compare using downlit (from `md_document`) in [this post](https://www.njtierney.com/post/2020/06/08/jq-rowwise-median/)

title: Hugo shortcodes are not preserved
description:
Examples:

- https://github.com/jemus42/hugodown-testing/blob/master/public/hugodown-rmarkdown/index.html#L179
- https://github.com/jemus42/hugodown-testing/blob/master/public/hugodown-rmarkdown/index.html#L286

I assume the issue is that `"` and `'` are replaced with `"` etc., where the page shows `{{< pkg “hugodown” >}}`.

I hope it's possible to work around this without having to resort to solutions like `blogdown::shortcode()`, which inserts preserving comments `<!--html_preserve-->` that do not work well with shortcodes that return inline-output (like a `<span>`), see the first example here https://github.com/jemus42/hugodown-testing/blob/master/public/hugodown-rmarkdown/index.html#L274-L279 which is displayed with additional linebreaks like [here](https://hugodown-testing.netlify.app/hugodown-rmarkdown/#inline).

Blogdown's `.Rmarkdown` format renders markdown which preserves shortcodes, see for example here: https://hugodown-testing.netlify.app/blogdown-rmarkdown/#shortcodes (source HTML [here](https://github.com/jemus42/hugodown-testing/blob/master/public/blogdown-rmarkdown/index.html), source `.Rmarkdown` [here](https://github.com/jemus42/hugodown-testing/blob/master/content/posts/rmarkdown-blogdown/index.Rmarkdown#L94)).


If the solution is a regex to detect/preserve shortcodes (I have not investigated what blogdown does there), please note that [there are two kinds of shortcodes](https://gohugo.io/content-management/shortcodes/) that may appear in the post source:

Shortcodes returning markdown: `{{% mdshortcode %}}`
Shortcodes returning HTML: `{{< htmlshortcode >}}`

title: Background color and image resolution for R figure output (CSS)
Code/Chunk output HTML structure differs from hugo/goldmark
description:
I am currently experimenting to see if I can easily switch from blogdown + `.Rmarkdown` to hugodown, and so far the first "issue" I have found is the chunk output.

I have prepared an [example hugo blog repo](https://github.com/jemus42/hugodown-testing) using the same theme I'm using for my blog without any CSS / layout modifications. It's auto-deployed to netlify at https://hugodown-testing.netlify.app/

I have started two blog posts, one using hugo+goldmark, and one using hugodown:
- Plain Markdown post: https://hugodown-testing.netlify.app/plain-markdown/
- Rmd post: https://hugodown-testing.netlify.app/hugodown-rmarkdown/

## Code output

I am assuming that the output of `hugodown_document` is intended to be as close to that of hugo/goldmark as possible, but where in the plain markdown / goldmark post, a code chunk looks like this:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1613346/83946677-9f143200-a812-11ea-889f-1286460911cc.png)
where code is contained in two nested `<div>`s:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1613346/83946713-d7b40b80-a812-11ea-8c41-05ee9a077b84.png)

…hugodown however produces this output:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1613346/83946742-fadebb00-a812-11ea-9fa8-862ffae421dc.png)
where the entire chunk is wrapped in `<pre class="chroma">`.

This leads to issues regarding the styling (margins, border-radius, probably why the colors differ?) in this particular theme, but I appreciate that this might not be a problem at all when using different themes (or using extra CSS).  

I hope it's possible to adjust this without having to account for site-specific goldmark settings (like line numbers and tabular display in my case).  
I would still like a solution where hugodown outputs code to a hugo `highlight` shortcode, but I assume that's not possible when downlit does the auto-linking / highlighting (which is very cool, I just tend to want to over-customize, and shortcodes give me a lot of flexibility across md + Rmd).

## Plot output 

Related to this are code chunks with plot output ([live example](https://hugodown-testing.netlify.app/hugodown-rmarkdown/#plots)):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1613346/83946806-5c068e80-a813-11ea-8c32-3417b62f8ad1.png)

Here the output figure is still contained in the above `<pre>`, causing the "code background color" — I assume this is not by design for some auto-linking/downlit-reason? If so, is there a way I can avoid this behavior?

title: hugo_document rendering is very long when hugo server is not started.
description:
While testing the new `hugo_document`  format, I observe a very long rendering time for very simple document when the hugo server is not started. 

I isolate the issue to be with the post processing part and specifically the active port checking. 
I takes a whole minute of real time.
``` r
bench::system_time(hugodown:::port_active(1313L))
#> process    real 
#>  62.5ms   1.02m
```

This is obviously due to the try with  `socketConnection`. There is a timeout that default to `getOption("timeout")` which is 60. see `?socketConnection`

If I change the option to like 5 second, it is more quicker... 5 sec. 
``` r
withr::with_options(list(timeout = 5), 
                    bench::system_time(hugodown:::port_active(1313L)))
#> process    real 
#> 78.12ms   5.07s
```

Maybe for a smoother user experience there could be smaller timeout set in hugodown to prevent this happening when the server is not started. 

Let's not that when the hugo server is started, it takes less than 1s to check, so rendering Rmd file is as usual.

title: site_root() should maybe not (only) rely on config.(toml|yaml)
description:
For hugo sites, it's quite possible the site root does not contain a `config.(toml|yaml)`, but rather a directory `config/` with subfolders corresponding to environments.  
See [the hugo docs](https://gohugo.io/getting-started/configuration/) for examples.

I personally use this approach with only a `config/_default` folder purely because theme- and site configuration can become quite crammed if done in a single file, and I like the ability to divide "hugo stuff" into `config/_default/config.toml` and have theme-specific settings in `config/_default/params.toml`.  

{blogdown} uses this same approach (determining site root by looking for `config.toml`), which is why I had to resort to a symlink.  
That's not a big deal of course, but if the scope of this package is specifically to work with hugo, it might be worth it to find a neater solution.

The problem is that, while every hugo site root has to contain a `config.*` file _or_ `config` folder, a `themes` directory and a `contents` directory — all these directory names can be configured arbitrarily (hugo options `configDir`, `themesDir`, `contentDir`).

The more I think about it, the more feasible it seems to just accept the minor caveat and expect a `config.(toml|yaml)`, but I at least wanted to throw the idea out there.
